blocks.text: **Meaning:** P(A | B) is the share of reference group B that also belongs to A. **Formula:** cases in both A and B / cases in B.

blocks.setup: Practice A, Q1: 25 commuters; 10 cycle. The full class has 40 students.

steps.label: Reference group
steps.text: Commuters (25), because the question asks about commuters.

steps.label: Report
steps.text: Give a percentage to one decimal place and name the reference group.

blocks.takeaway: P(cycle | commuter) uses commuters in the denominator; reversing the condition changes the reference group.

blocks.text: Assumptions from Notes §1.4: equally weighted cases; reference group is not empty.

blocks.prompt: Prior attempt: a column percentage was computed using the row total.
blocks.first_error: Selected the row total as denominator.
blocks.fix: Use the total of the column containing the cell. First say which group is the reference group; that group's total is the denominator.
blocks.conditions: Percentages down a column sum to 100%; across a row they need not.

blocks.text: Reporting rule: percentage to 1 decimal place + reference group in words (for example, “40.0% of commuters”). (Outline; Notes §2)

The current outline lists Bayes’ rule in scope, but its teaching notes are not posted (profile source register; Outline). This guide cannot supply a course-grounded rule or worked method yet. Review the lecture notes when available.
Split cases by a categorical variable and compute one summary (such as a mean or count) per group. Result: one row per non-empty group, not per original case. (Notes §3.1–3.2)
Compare groups using the same summary; do not compare a group mean with a group total. (Notes §3.3)
